Convex hull.subject: Applied Sciences
Convex hull.question: The _____ was Smallest convex set containing a given set.
Convex hull.fact: In geometry, the convex hull, convex envelope or convex closure of a shape is the smallest convex set that contains it. The convex hull may be defined either as the intersection of all convex sets containing a given subset of a Euclidean space, or equivalently as the set of all convex combinations of points in the subset.

Convex hull.subject: Applied Sciences

Convex hull.fact: Instead, the compactness of convex hulls of compact sets, in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, is generalized by the Krein–Smulian theorem, according to which the closed convex hull of a weakly compact subset of a Banach space (a subset that is compact under the weak topology) is weakly compact. According to the Krein–Milman theorem, every compact convex set in a Euclidean space (or more generally in a locally convex topological vector space) is the convex hull of its extreme points.

Convex metric space.question: The _____ was Type of metric space in mathematics.
Convex metric space.fact: Any convex set in a Euclidean space is a convex metric space with the induced Euclidean norm. For closed sets the converse is also true: if a closed subset of a Euclidean space together with the induced distance is a convex metric space, then it is a convex set (this is a particular case of a more general statement to be discussed below).

Convex metric space.subject: Applied Sciences
Convex metric space.question: A metric space is called convex (or _____-convex or M-convex) if, for any two distinct points x and y in X, there exists a third point z in X lying between x and y
Convex metric space.fact: A metric space is called convex (or Menger-convex or M-convex) if, for any two distinct points x and y in X, there exists a third point z in X lying between x and y.

Convex metric space.subject: Applied Sciences
Convex metric space.question: Metric convexity defined this way does not have one of the most important properties of _____ convex sets: the intersection of two convex sets is convex
Convex metric space.fact: It is then natural to think of convex metric spaces as generalizing the notion of convexity beyond Euclidean spaces, with usual linear segments replaced by metric segments. Metric convexity defined this way does not have one of the most important properties of Euclidean convex sets: the intersection of two convex sets is convex.

Convex metric space.subject: Applied Sciences
Convex metric space.question: This is stronger than the original _____ convexity, as it is not satisfied with just one point between x and y, but requires a continuum of points - one for every real number in [0, d(x,y)]
Convex metric space.fact: A metric space (X,d) is called Strongly Menger convex if for any two distinct points x and y in X, and for every number r between 0 and d(x,y), there exists a third point z in X lying between x and y, such that d(x,z)=r. This is stronger than the original Menger convexity, as it is not satisfied with just one point between x and y, but requires a continuum of points - one for every real number in [0, d(x,y)].

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: The _____ was Component of a database management system.
Database engine.fact: A database engine (or storage engine) is the underlying software component that a database management system (DBMS) uses to create, read, update and delete (CRUD) data from a database. The term "database engine" is frequently used interchangeably with "database server" or "database management system".

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: For example, MySQL supports _____DB as well as MyISAM
Database engine.fact: For example, MySQL supports InnoDB as well as MyISAM.

Database engine.question: An operating _____ always utilizes several storage types simultaneously

Database transaction.subject: Applied Sciences
Database transaction.question: The _____ was Unit of work performed within a database management system.

Database transaction.question: A distributed transaction enforces the _____ properties over multiple nodes, and might include systems such as databases, storage managers, file systems, messaging systems, and other data managers
